Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap of requirements (as I understood them):
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end user-facing latency <= 200ms for short responses (avg ~60 tokens).
- Streaming use case for live triage: per-token streaming latency target p95 <= 50ms after first token.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 requests/sec, expected peak bursts to 600 reqs/sec for ~5–10 minutes.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency ~40–60.
- Accuracy/quality: must match current baseline model (they're testing against OpenAI gpt-3.5-like outputs).

Attachments: you mentioned you'd share a traffic sample (timestamps, request sizes) — if you can drop that CSV we'll run a quick capacity estimate and propose cost/performance levers.

Initial levers we plan to evaluate (high level):
- Continuous batching tuned to your latency SLOs to increase throughput without violating p95.
- Prefix/KV caching for common prompts to reduce token compute on repeat queries.
- Quantization profiles (int8 / group-quant) for candidate model variants to reduce latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Model variants: consider a lower-latency 13B quantized model for streaming, fallback to 70B for quality-critical paths.

Next steps:
1) Can you share the traffic sample and a representative prompt set (zenova_traffic_sample.csv)?
2) I'll loop in Vivek to scope a short Proof-of-Concept load test (we typically do a 48–72h run with your sample traffic).
3) We'll deliver a Performance Matrix (expected p50/p95, throughput, cost estimate across options) — target by EOD Friday if we get the sample today.

If anything above looks off, flag it and I'll update. Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. Attaching the traffic sample and a short prompt set we use for triage. A few clarifications: 

- The 200ms p95 is a hard internal target for the UI shell that shows a single-step suggested action. For multi-turn flows we can tolerate up to 400ms p95.
- Streaming is critical for the clinical triage flow — clinicians must see tokens appear as they're generated (we measure perceived latency). Ideally first token arrives in <50ms after request acceptance.
- Peak bursts are driven by shift changes (7am/7pm). Bursts can last up to 12 minutes but are typically spiky — see column "burst_window" in the CSV.
- Quality: we can accept a minor drop if it reduces latency significantly, but we need a simple A/B plan during POC to verify.

Files attached: zenova_traffic_sample.csv, zenova_prompt_set.json

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample — this is exactly what we need. High-level plan and assumptions before we kick off POC: 

Proposed POC scope (48–72h):
- Run load tests against a sandbox endpoint using your provided traffic pattern (we'll emulate bursts and steady state).
- Baseline: measure p50/p95 latency and token-streaming latency for a small, medium, and large model variant.
- Evaluate levers: continuous batching params, KV/prefix caching effectiveness, and two quantization profiles (int8 and gf16 -> int8), and an 8-bit/4-bit mixed profile if helpful.
- Deliverables: Performance Matrix (p50/p95 streaming & non-streaming, throughput, estimated $/1M tokens), recommended config (batch size, max-concurrency, cache TTL, quant profile), and a risk/rollback plan.

Preliminary recommended configs (subject to POC):
- Streaming-first path: 13B quantized model (int8) with small batch sizes (2–8) and aggressive early-token streaming optimizations. Expected p95 streaming token latency ~30–60ms; user perceived latency << 200ms for short replies.
- High-quality path: 70B or 34B model with group-quant and prefix caching, batched for throughput (batch sizes 8–32), targeted p95 non-streaming latency ~200–350ms depending on token count.
- Caching: 20–40% hit rate expected for templated prompts based on your CSV — KV cache TTL of 30s for short-term reuse.
- Cost levers: quantization reduces GPU memory and per-token core usage (~2–3x cost reduction vs FP16 at modest quality loss), continuous batching can reduce per-token cost by 20–40% at the expense of tail latency if not tuned.

Ask from you:
1) Confirm we can run a sandbox endpoint hitting a zone in us-west with ~200–600 reqs/sec (we'll provide exact IPs and test accounts).
2) Procurement: if you need an MSA/PO to start the POC, can procurement share a typical POC window/terms?
3) Any redlines re: data handling — we plan to keep logs for POC only and can sign an NDA if needed.

Once you confirm, Vivek and I will schedule the run. I've included Vivek for the test plan/timeline.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Claire — quick technical note and scheduling options from my side.

Technical notes:
- For streaming-first flows we'll enable chunked token delivery and tune the kernel prefetch to prioritize first-token latencies. That usually means smaller initial beam/window and an early flush to the socket.
- Continuous batching strategy: use dynamic batching with SLAs — i.e., we start with small batch thresholds and expand during steady state. We'll instrument an adaptive batch controller to back off batch formation during detected spikes to protect p95.
- Caching: we'll run an offline analysis on the sample to estimate prefix hit-rate; if templated prompts represent >15% of traffic we'll recommend a dedicated LRU cache layer with a short TTL.
- Quantization: will test both static int8 and adaptive group-wise quant to find the sweet spot for quality vs latency. We'll include quality regression checks against your prompt set.

Scheduling: I can run the POC starting Monday 2026-06-22 if we get confirmation + access by EOD Friday. Typical run cadence:
- Day 0: sandbox setup + warmup
- Day 1–2: run burst/steady-state scenarios and capture traces
- Day 3: analysis and Performance Matrix delivery

If procurement needs an SOW or limited-time dedicated capacity, we can attach a short POC addendum.

Claire — can you confirm access and whether we should include a HIPAA addendum? If yes, we'll pull legal on a simple one-way DPA for logs.
